meaning:
μακράν (prop. fem. accusative of μακρός, Sc. ὁδόν), adv. ,
[in LXX for רָחוֹק hi., רָחַק, etc. ;]
a long way, far: Luk.15:20, Act.22:21; before ἀπό, Mat.8:30, Luk.7:6, Jhn.21:8, Act.17:27; id. metaphorically, Mrk.12:34; οἱ εἰς μ., Act.2:39 (cf. Isa.2:2); metaphorically, οἱ ποτὲ ὄντες μ. (opposite to ἐγγύς), Eph.2:13; οἱ μ., Eph.2:17.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from them.
When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from God’s Kingdom.” No one dared ask him any question after that.
Jesus went with them. When he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, “Lord, don’t trouble yourself, for I am not…
But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish.
For the promise is to you, and to your children, and to all who are far off, even as many as the Lord our God will call to himself.”
But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Christ.
